_readme: Residential electricity rates for the Caribbean cost pages. Edit a country's rate, date and source here and every Caribbean page updates. localRate is per kWh in the local currency; usdRate is the same in US dollars at the source's exchange rate. `basis` says in plain words what each rate includes (all-in average, or a utility's per-kWh charges for a stated monthly use before fixed charges); it is shown under the Caribbean table and on each country page. Each country uses its newest available figure, so dates differ between countries (see asOf).

countries.name: Bahamas
countries.source: BPL residential tariff and fuel charge on a September 2026 household bill (1,505 kWh; energy and fuel charges, before fixed charges and taxes)
countries.basis: Energy and fuel charges for a 1,505 kWh month, before fixed charges and VAT
countries.note: BPL bills residential energy in tiers, plus a fuel charge that is a direct pass-through of fuel costs. On a September 2026 bill: no energy charge on the first 200 kWh, 11.95¢/kWh from 201 to 800 kWh and 14.95¢ above 800, plus a fuel charge of 17.4¢/kWh on the first 800 kWh and 21.4¢ above that. So every kWh above 800 a month (usually the air conditioning) costs 36.35¢ before fixed charges and taxes, more than the 31.0¢ average shown here.

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.source: GlobalPetrolPrices.com, household electricity price (includes fuel charge, taxes and fees)
countries.basis: All-in household average: fuel charge, taxes and fees included
countries.note: JPS bills include a fuel charge that changes every month (J$26.78/kWh in August 2026, down from J$33.01 in March) plus a purchased-power charge, so the effective rate moves with world fuel prices. GCT on household electricity was cut to 7% in May 2025. The rate shown is the newest complete all-in figure available (June 2025); JPS doesn't publish a single all-in rate.

countries.name: Barbados
countries.source: BL&P domestic tariff (base energy charges) plus the September 2026 fuel clause adjustment of 37.53¢/kWh and VAT at 17.5%, for a 1,000 kWh month, before the customer charge
countries.basis: Energy charge, fuel charge and VAT for a 1,000 kWh month, before the monthly customer charge
countries.note: BL&P's base energy charge rises with usage (BBD 0.160/kWh for the first 150 kWh up to BBD 0.254 above 1,500 kWh), and a fuel clause adjustment set monthly (37.53¢ in September 2026) is added to every kWh. Barbados has at times charged a reduced 7.5% VAT on the first 250 kWh of household use, which would lower the average slightly.

countries.name: Trinidad and Tobago
countries.source: GlobalPetrolPrices.com, household electricity price (includes taxes and fees)
countries.basis: All-in household average: taxes and fees included
countries.note: Trinidad and Tobago generates its power from domestic natural gas, which is why its rates are among the lowest in the Caribbean. We found no change to T&TEC's residential rates since this figure (a proposed increase from the Regulated Industries Commission was still awaiting a government decision in 2025), so this June 2025 figure is the newest available.

countries.name: Cayman Islands
countries.source: CUC standard billing rates (from June 1, 2026) with the fuel cost charge capped at CI$0.18/kWh by the government relief programme, plus fuel duty and renewables charge, for the average household (1,158 kWh a month), before the facilities charge
countries.basis: Energy, capped fuel charge, duty and renewables charge for a 1,158 kWh month, before the facilities charge
countries.note: CUC's energy charge is CI$0.1387/kWh, and the fuel cost charge is capped at CI$0.18/kWh on usage from 101 to 2,000 kWh a month under a government relief programme that runs through December 2026. When the cap ends, the fuel charge goes back to CUC's monthly fuel cost (about CI$0.24/kWh in October 2026), which would put the average near CI$0.41/kWh. Fuel duty, a renewables charge and, above 1,000 kWh, a licence fee are added per kWh.

countries.name: Bermuda
countries.source: BELCO residential tariff (base rates from August 1, 2026; fuel adjustment rate 14.226¢ from October 1, 2026; Regulatory Authority fee), for a 1,000 kWh month, before the facilities charge
countries.basis: Energy, fuel and regulatory charges for a 1,000 kWh month, before the facilities charge
countries.note: BELCO charges by usage block: 14.52¢/kWh for the first 250 kWh, 25.61¢ from 251 to 700 and 39.50¢ above 700, plus the fuel adjustment (14.226¢) and a small regulatory fee on every kWh. So once a summer bill passes 700 kWh, each extra kWh the AC uses costs about 54.3¢, well above the 41.8¢ average shown here. A monthly facilities charge ($31 to $149, by daily usage) is on top.

countries.name: Puerto Rico
countries.source: Puerto Rico Energy Bureau quarterly adjustment, as reported by El Nuevo Día (Oct. 1, 2026)
countries.basis: Residential cost per kWh for the quarter, after the Energy Bureau's quarterly fuel and purchased-power adjustment
countries.note: The Energy Bureau resets fuel and purchased-power charges every quarter. The October–December 2026 rate is a record high for residential customers.

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.source: GlobalPetrolPrices.com, household electricity price (includes taxes and fees)
countries.basis: All-in household average: taxes and fees included
countries.note: Dominican residential tariffs are set by the government and rise in steps with monthly usage, so households running AC heavily pay a higher rate on their top block than the average shown here. This September 2025 figure is the newest published all-in rate.
